chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ahwal, from Sallam ibn Al-Mustanir, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrate: 'When the Qaim arises, he will present Faith to every Nasibi (Hostile One). If they enter it truly, [he accepts them]; otherwise, he will strike his neck, or he will pay the Jizyah just as the People of the Book (Ahl al-Dhimma) pay it today, and a strap will be tied around his waist, and he will be taken out from the cities to the dark places (al-Sawad).'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Book (Christians and Jews)
key_terms.الْهِمْيَانُ: A strap worn around the waist as a sign
key_terms.الْوَاصِبِ: Nasibi (one who is hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the Nasibi when Al-Qaim rises according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia eschatology, this hadith outlines the political and social restructuring by Al-Qaim, who distinguishes between true believers and the Nasibi (enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt) by offering them a choice between genuine acceptance of faith or the penalty of death. For those who choose the latter, the imposition of Jizyah with the Himyan strap and exile from urban centers to the countryside serves as a tangible sign of their subordination, reflecting the historical precedent of Dhimmi status but applied specifically to the Ahl al-Bayt's adversaries.
